subject: Two Packrat Libraries in one RStudio Project?

messages.author: 31a23ff88538287b
messages.subject: Two Packrat Libraries in one RStudio Project?
parts:
Hello,

As I have been testing the RStudio 0.99.1285, I have noticed a few things with Packrat that I'm not quite sure if they should be happenning or not. In my project, I currently have two Packrat libraries, which probably should not be happening. It could be because I have upgraded my R version from 3.3.0 to 3.3.1, and I think Packrat has maybe attempted to load both the folders with the lock file. 

I've also noticed some issues with trying to remove packages from my library, and I can't seem to figure out why I can't remove a package from my session..

Lastly, I've installed a package from CRAN, but in Packrat it does not show where it comes from, nor can I reinstall or remove it from my session. Thoughts on how to proceed moving forward?
I have attached my session info, as I'm not really sure where to start with diagnosing these issues, as well as the packrat lock file.

Thank you Kevin for all the hard work you have put into Packrat. Not trying to bash on it, but just to give some feedback on some issues I have experienced.

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Two Packrat Libraries in one RStudio Project?
parts:
Interesting; thanks. It looks like the libraries as set by packrat are what we would expect, so I'm curious why RStudio is reporting something inconsistent with the current library paths.

Does explicitly refreshing the packages pane help? There should be a little refresh icon near the top-right of the packages pane that you can click to refresh the package listing.

It's also possible that (as you said) the package 'brew' is showing up in the packages pane as it's detected as a dependency of a currently installed package, even though it itself is not currently installed. If you execute 'packrat::status()', does it report something to that effect? (The package 'brew' is required by your project but is not installed, or something to that effect)
